evidence_kind: original public execution receipt; private raw capture not republished by this review
body:
Actual-Q9 CPU qualification completed for `586fe4c44eb21ddd4670fb9f1b3099b775219caa` on Linux x86_64 / Python 3.12.3, LOTUS 1.2.4 and Transformers 4.57.6, restricted to CPU 0–7. This resolves the earlier replay-capacity intake blocker: actual allowances were 2 MiB per item for input/result, 272 MiB aggregate input and window 136.

The unchanged SemBench Q9 initial Map selection supplied its first 128 occurrences, without deduplication (99 distinct complete messages: 29 repeated twice and 70 once). Five native formatter/local-tokenizer captures passed full-message/token stability and all three frame-size comparisons. Three arms then each received one CPU warm-up and five interleaved timed replays; complete wire content, batch members, tokens and fixed placeholder assembly agreed. No model answers or accuracy were generated.

| Complete CPU replay, median | Time |
|---|---:|
| Original sizing | 47.897 ms |
| Direct JSON control | 36.468 ms |
| Message-length reuse | 47.249 ms |

Reuse is 1.35% faster than the original but **29.56% slower than direct JSON**, so it fails the stated simple-control stop condition. Stop this candidate at CPU engineering evidence; do not escalate to GPU.

Original sizing occupied a median 12.81% of the captured serial preparation slice. That denominator includes formatter, prepared validation, native tokenization and envelope construction, and excludes source/LM/tokenizer setup, Core payload coding, actual emission and persistence. The first capture is retained separately; the following four slices span 8.338 ms, while their median complete original-sizing cost is 17.228 ms. The alternative hypothetical-total-elimination-versus-variation stop condition is therefore not established by that warm-slice range; the direct-JSON failure is sufficient. Replay uses recorded tokens and is not native-tokenizer or GPU time.

All five capture samples and all 15 measured replays, including slow samples, are retained privately. One private observation-wrapper import error occurred after successful preflight and before any capture/replay; it was retained, only that import was corrected, and preflight was reused. Candidate source and dependencies were unchanged. Model calls, Ray runtime and GPU work were zero; observed owned processes exited, no new SHM remained, and the host lease was released. Keep this PR draft and unmerged; these measurements establish no whole-query, DAG or GPU benefit.
